description.text: The bZIP YAP family of transcription factors is involved in the regulation of oxidative stress response, redox homeostasis, and various stress responses, including resistance to toxic compounds like arsenic and antifungal drugs. Members of the family activate the transcription of genes encoding antioxidant enzymes, components of the cellular thiol-reducing pathways, and multidrug transporters. They are characterized by their ability to bind to specific DNA core binding sites, and their activity is modulated by the oxidation state of cysteine-rich domains, which affects their subcellular localization. Some members also play roles in iron regulation, metabolism control, and cell cycle regulation.
